correction.text: Tripoli and its surroundings: 'Their territory comprised Tripoli and its surroundings in present-day Libya' (the Tripolitanian part of Cliopatria's 1713 shape)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the two years before Cliopatria's row: the page has Ahmed Karamanli seizing the throne in the 1711 coup (29 July 1711 in the ruler list). The Gulf of Sidra and Cyrenaican coast in the 1713 shape are added by the 1713 gain; the page gives no year for 'persuading the Ottomans to recognize him as governor'. The infobox has no area.

85,534 km2, 1713-1756: a coastal strip from Tripoli to Cyrenaica (89 Cyrenaican cells) with a 30-cell strip in what is now south-east Tunisia. The page says only that Ahmed expanded control 'as far as Fezzan and Cyrenaica' before 1745 (no year) and gives no area; the Tunisian strip is on no page opened (the civil-war page has Djerba under Tunis in 1794) and is left unverified, as is the Libyan interior, which stays outside the shape until the 1807 keyframe.
85,483 km2, 1757-1761: 51 km2 smaller than the shapes either side, a boundary-vector artefact. The page records no border move in the reign of Ali I (1754-1793).
85,534 km2, 1762-1793, identical to 1713. The page has no event for these decades.

76,381 km2, 1794-1795: the 30-cell Tunisian strip is dropped. The civil-war page says nothing about a frontier strip (only that Burghul 'occupied Djerba on 30 September 1794', an island under Tunis), so the loss is carried at confidence 1 and matches the gain in the beylik-of-tunis dossier. The Ottoman-backed Burghul held Tripoli from 30 July 1793 to 19 January 1795; Cliopatria keeps drawing the Karamanlis; the ledger's loss and gain against ali-burghul (a rebel-type dossier, rule 5) carry Tripoli's 18 months under the usurper.

correction.text: unchanged for 1796-1806: the coastal strip from Tripoli to Cyrenaica without Fezzan and the Cyrenaican interior

The Fezzan page lists full occupations 'in 1679-1682, 1690, 1716, 1718 and 1811/1812' without naming the occupier; the Karamanli page has Yusuf bringing 'the Fezzan under direct control' by 1807 and the Fezzan bey al-Mukni acting for him in 1817. The 1811 year is the Fezzan page's.

Both pages end the dynasty in 1835: 'In 1835 the Ottomans reestablished direct control' (Ottoman Tripolitania) and Ali II's reign ends '26 May 1835' (Karamanli). No page opened has a Karamanli remnant in the east to 1839, so the years belong to ottoman-tripolitania.

region.text: Tripoli and its surroundings: 'Their territory comprised Tripoli and its surroundings in present-day Libya'

ledger.note: 1711: Ahmed Karamanli seizes Tripoli and founds the dynasty. He 'murdered the Ottoman governor of Tripolitania and seized the throne in the 1711 Karamanli coup', then persuaded the Ottomans to recognize him as governor (no year given) and made the post hereditary; the ruler list dates his reign from 29 July 1711.

region.text: the Gulf of Sidra, the Cyrenaican coast and a strip of south-east Tunisia added to the Tripoli core in Cliopatria's 1713 shape

ledger.note: 1713: the dynasty's coast reaches Cyrenaica. The page says Ahmed expanded control 'as far as Fezzan and Cyrenaica' before his death in 1745 and gives no year; 1713 is Cliopatria's start, when its Ottoman Empire row gives up the Libyan coast and the south-east Tunisian strip.

region.text: Tripoli, from which Ali Burghul expelled the Karamanli on 30 July 1793

ledger.note: 30 July 1793: Ali Burghul takes Tripoli (a usurper regime, drawn as a rebel state). He entered Tripolitania on 29 July 1793 with nine merchant ships and about 300 mercenaries, expelled 'Ali ibn Mehmed Karamanli on 30 July and 'would rule it in the name of the sultan'; Panzac calls him 'an Algerian usurper who claimed to be supported by the sultan'.

region.text: the strip of south-east Tunisia (Medenine to Zarzis) in Cliopatria's Karamanli shape up to 1793

ledger.note: 1794: a strip on the Tripolitanian frontier passes to Tunis. The page is silent about any cession (it says only that Burghul 'occupied Djerba on 30 September 1794'); the year is Cliopatria's, whose Karamanli shape loses 30 cells of south-east Tunisia in 1794, and the Tunis dossier records the matching gain at confidence 1.

region.text: Tripoli, regained by Hamet and Yusuf Karamanli

ledger.note: 19 January 1795: the Karamanli return to Tripoli and the usurper is crushed. 'Hamet and Yusuf returned to Tripoli' on 19 January 1795 'with the aid of the Bey of Tunis and the rebels' and Burghul fled to Egypt; Hamet ruled from 20 January until Yusuf deposed him on 11 June 1795. The Karamanli page dates the return January 1794; the civil-war page's January 1795 follows its own account of Hammuda acting after 30 September 1794.

region.text: Derna, on the Cyrenaican coast, captured by the American-led force

ledger.note: April 1805: the Battle of Derna. William Eaton and Presley O'Bannon led 'eight Marines' and about 500 mercenaries across the desert from Alexandria to capture Derna, in support of the exiled Hamet Karamanli (Eaton's backing of Hamet is on the Karamanli page); the page dates the battle 'April-May 1805'.

region.text: Derna, the only ground taken in the war

ledger.note: June 1805: the First Barbary War ends. Yusuf Karamanli signed the treaty 'ending hostilities on 10 June 1805' (the page's infobox says 4 June); the United States paid $60,000 for the prisoners. The page does not say what became of Derna and Hamet.

ledger.note: 1807: Cyrenaica submits. 'By 1807 Yusuf had forced "all the tribes of Cyrenaica and the Fezzan" to submit'; the year is the page's terminus; the page speaks of tribes, so 'nobody' as counterpart is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Fezzan within the Ottoman Tripolitania shape of 1840, the Murzuk sanjak

ledger.note: 1807: Fezzan submits to Tripoli. The same sentence has the tribes 'of the Fezzan' forced to submit, and the page adds that Yusuf 'brought the Fezzan under direct control'; the Fezzan page has the occupation in 1811/1812, so the two steps are dated 1807 (submission) and 1811 (occupation).

region.text: Fezzan within the Ottoman Tripolitania shape of 1840, the Murzuk sanjak

ledger.note: 1811: Fezzan is occupied. The Fezzan page lists full occupations 'in 1679-1682, 1690, 1716, 1718 and 1811/1812' without naming the occupier; the Karamanli page mentions 'the Fezzan bey al-Mukni' aiding al-Kanimi in 1817 and has expeditions in 1821.

region.text: Fezzan within the Ottoman Tripolitania shape of 1840, the Murzuk sanjak

ledger.note: 1811: Fezzan comes under direct rule from Tripoli, 'occupied in 1811/1812' on the Fezzan page (no occupier named); the Karamanli page has trans-Saharan expeditions in 1821 and Yusuf dropping his plan to conquer Bornu in 1824.

ledger.note: 1835: the Karamanli dynasty falls. 'In 1835 the government of Sultan Mahmud II took advantage of local disturbances to reassert their direct authority'; 'In 1835, the Ottomans reestablished direct control over the region until its annexation by Italy in 1912.'

wars.name: Tripolitanian civil war

zones.text: Tripoli, held by Ali Burghul from 30 July 1793 to 19 January 1795

wars.outcome: Karamanli victory: Hamet and Yusuf returned to Tripoli on 19 January 1795 with the aid of the Bey of Tunis and the rebels; Burghul fled to Egypt.
wars.note: The infobox dates the war July 1790 - 20 January 1795; the page gives Yusuf's open rebellion as June 1791 in one section and June 1793 in another, and the Karamanli page puts the return in January 1794.

wars.name: First Barbary War
wars.outcome: Peace of 10 June 1805 (infobox: 4 June); $60,000 for the American prisoners; no territorial change recorded.
wars.note: Per the Karamanli page Yusuf 'unofficially declare[d] war, in May 1801, by chopping down the flagpole'; the USS Philadelphia was captured in October 1803. The page does not say whether Derna was held after the treaty.

wars.name: Karamanli civil war and Ottoman return

zones.text: Tripoli, from which the Ottomans 'deposed and exiled Ali II'

wars.outcome: Yusuf abdicated in 1832 for his son Ali II; 'civil war soon resulted' and Mahmud II's troops deposed Ali II in 1835 and reestablished direct control.
wars.note: The Ottoman landing date is not on either page; 26 May 1835 is the end of Ali II's reign in the ruler list. Rebel claimants (Mehmed Karamanli, Mehmed ibn Ali) are listed for 1817-1835.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on the pages: the coastal frontier with Tunis was not fixed until 1886 (Libya-Tunisia border page, read for the ottoman-tripolitania dossier) and the Saharan, Fezzan and Cyrenaican limits are tribal.

notes: Karamanli dynasty (af-02-f). (1) Start/end: the page gives the coup of 29 July 1711 and the end of Ali II's reign on 26 May 1835 (the infobox's 'Deposition: 1832' is Yusuf's abdication); Cliopatria runs 1713-1839. Cliopatria's Ottoman Empire row covers the Libyan coast (544 cells) and a 30-cell strip of south-east Tunisia up to 1712 and 87 Tripolitanian cells again in 1836-1839: the ottoman-empire dossier (me-10) should drop them for 1711-1712 (Karamanli) and 1835-1839 (ottoman-tripolitania). (2) The Cliopatria Karamanli shape is only a coastal strip (Fezzan 0 cells); the 1807 and 1811 keyframes widen it to the shape of the Ottoman Tripolitania of 1840 north of Kufra on the strength of the page's 'covering most of Libya', and Fezzan is a vassal from 1807 and occupied from 1811 (Fezzan page 1811/1812 against the Karamanli page's 'direct control' by 1807; both kept). (3) The 30-cell Tunisian strip in the 1713-1793 shape and its loss in 1794 are on no page: the civil-war page has Burghul occupying Djerba on 30 September 1794 and says nothing of a frontier strip. Confidence 1; the Tunis dossier's matching gain is also confidence 1. (4) The Karamanli page dates the restoration January 1794; the civil-war page 19 January 1795 and the ruler list agrees with 1795. (5) Not on any page opened (budget): the Ottoman recognition year (Cliopatria 1713), the 1830s Tunisian and Ottoman moves, Ghadames and Wadai relations, the Treaty of 1815 episodes. Gazetteer: all names resolved; Derna and Tripoli are radii.
